id: assign-labor
title: "Assign an associate to a path"
description: "Puts an associate on pathId for a new interval, raising LaborAssigned (first assignment) or LaborReassigned (an assignment was already active). The 'exactly one ACTIVE assignment per associate' invariant is enforced by construction, not by rejecting a second call: if the associate already has an active assignment, it is closed first (its hours are logged against the associate's shift) and the new one starts — this matches how rebalancing actually happens on the floor, a supervisor moves someone without first 'unassigning' them. The assignment requires the associate hold the path's required certification (by convention, the Certification with the same name as the PathId — e.g. path 'pack' requires certification 'pack'), and is rejected if the associate is currently on a logged break or their shift has ended. Because each call closes the prior interval and raises an event, a blind retry would double-apply it, so this route is protected by the Idempotency-Key header (ADR-0027): a retried request with the same key and body replays the first response."

>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/associates/{id}/assignments"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Puts an associate on pathId for a new interval, raising LaborAssigned (first assignment) or LaborReassigned (an assignment was already active). The "exactly one ACTIVE assignment per associate" invariant is enforced by construction, not by rejecting a second call: if the associate already has an active assignment, it is closed first (its hours are logged against the associate's shift) and the new one starts — this matches how rebalancing actually happens on the floor, a supervisor moves someone without first "unassigning" them. The assignment requires the associate hold the path's required certification (by convention, the Certification with the same name as the PathId — e.g. path "pack" requires certification "pack"), and is rejected if the associate is currently on a logged break or their shift has ended. Because each call closes the prior interval and raises an event, a blind retry would double-apply it, so this route is protected by the Idempotency-Key header (ADR-0027): a retried request with the same key and body replays the first response.

Clients MUST always send a non-empty value on the routes that declare it: a deployment backed by Postgres (every real deployment) rejects a request without it with 400 idempotency-key-required. It is declared optional here only because the in-memory development mode (which the contract test boots) does not enforce it. Reuse the SAME key for retries of one logical request (same body) — the first response, success or business error, is stored and replayed byte-for-byte for the key's TTL (24h by default) — and a NEW key for each new logical request. Reusing a key with a different body is rejected with 422 idempotency-key-reused.","schema":{"type":"string"},"example":"3f1d6a4e-9c0b-4a39-8f0f-5b2d1c7e9a10"}]}
